subject: Log snapshot handover checklist and export options
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@finvera.com>

Subject: Snapshot handover: formats, manifest, and deletion attestations

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. As part of our procurement/legal review we need a short checklist and example artifacts for how Redwood would hand over tenant audit/access logs for Finvera (for a one-time handback). Specifically the security team asked for:

- Supported export formats (CSV/JSON/Parquet) and sample payloads
- How timestamps/timezones are represented and whether original ingestion IDs are preserved
- Manifest (file-level metadata) format and checksum approach (MD5/SHA256)
- Encryption in transit + at-rest for the handover bundle
- Typical lead time to produce a complete snapshot and any available SLA for delivery
- Evidence that deleted records are irretrievable after the requested deletion window (attestation approach)

We attached a short spec (snapshot_spec_v1.pdf) with the fields they’re expecting. Can you share a checklist and an example manifest or sample file? Also please include whether you can push directly to an S3 bucket in our account vs. secure SFTP/Share.

If helpful, loop in your infra/ops folks.

Appreciate it — Samira
Security Operations
Finvera

Attachment: snapshot_spec_v1.pdf

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Snapshot handover: formats, manifest, and deletion attestations

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the clear spec. I've created a concise handover checklist and attached a draft we typically share with customers (redwood_snapshot_handover_checklist_v2.docx). Quick summary below — full details are in the attachment.

1) Supported formats and samples
 - Primary: gzipped Parquet (preferred for large volumes, preserves schema)
 - Alternate: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) or CSV (schema-limited)
 - We include a small sample Parquet + a JSON manifest with per-file metadata and checksums (we've included a sample manifest: parquet-sample-manifest.json).

2) Timestamps & identifiers
 - Timestamps are exported in ISO-8601 UTC (e.g., 2026-09-07T16:12:34Z).
 - Original ingestion IDs (event_id / trace_id fields) are preserved where available and included in the export schema.

3) Manifest & checksums
 - Manifest is JSON array of objects: {filename, start_ts, end_ts, record_count, md5, size_bytes}.
 - We compute MD5 for each file and an overall SHA256 on the compressed bundle for end-to-end verification.

4) Encryption and transfer options
 - At-rest: AES-256 for stored snapshots on our staging bucket.
 - In-transit: TLS 1.2+ for transfers.
 - Delivery options:
    • Direct S3 PUT into your pre-provisioned bucket (we rotate temporary credentials scoped to the job).
    • SFTP over FTPS to an endpoint you control.
    • Customer-controlled air-gapped handoff (on-prem disk; by special arrangement).

5) Lead time and SLA
 - Typical lead time: 5-8 business days for a 30-day window (volume-dependent).
 - For larger windows (6+ months) add 3–5 business days per additional month of data.
 - We can commit a delivery SLA for Enterprise contracts; otherwise we provide estimated ETA per request.

6) Deletion attestation
 - We provide a signed deletion attestation describing the deletion workflow and retention tombstone. For legal holds, we can provide a chain-of-custody export and an internal audit log slice showing deletion events.

Next steps
 - If S3 delivery is preferred, please share the bucket name and a minimal IAM policy we should assume (we create scoped temporary creds).
 - If you need a formal SLA/statement of work we will loop Legal (Marissa).

Looping in Karthik to confirm export file layout and any technical constraints.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Security Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_snapshot_handover_checklist_v2.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Snapshot handover: formats, manifest, and deletion attestations

Hi Samira / team —

Filling in the technical specifics Evelyn summarized. Apologies for the slightly dense note — intent is to avoid ambiguity on the export payload.

Export layout (example):
- manifest.json (top-level)
  [
    {"filename":"logs_20260901_0001.parquet.gz","start_ts":"2026-09-01T00:00:00Z","end_ts":"2026-09-01T23:59:59Z","record_count":125432,"md5":"b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184","size_bytes":12345678}
  ]

- logs_*.parquet.gz (snappy compression inside Parquet), each file limited to ~250MB compressed to make streaming/parallel download easier
- checksums: md5 per file; bundle SHA256 for integrity

Timestamp notes:
- All exported timestamps normalized to UTC to avoid cross-region ambiguity. Source local tz is preserved in a "local_ts" field if you need it.

Retention / deletion specifics:
- When a deletion request is processed, we mark the records as tombstones and remove logically from the live dataset.
- For export handovers, we only include records that are present in the tenant's live set as of the snapshot time; deleted records prior to the snapshot are excluded.
- If you require an export that includes historical deleted records for e-discovery, we can run a separate extract but that requires a legal hold and an extended timeframe (adds ~5 business days).

Delivery mechanics:
- S3: we perform multipart uploads and publish object-level metadata (x-amz-meta-source-window). We will provide limited-scope STS creds valid for 48 hours by default.
- SFTP: we checksum files server-side and place a manifest in the root of the transfer.

Operational checklist we follow (high-level):
1) Scope confirmation (time window, accounts, object types)
2) Cost estimate + approval (data egress and staging costs)
3) Provision staging bucket / transfer endpoint
4) Dry-run on a small window (sample files + manifest)
5) Full snapshot job + verification
6) Delivery + signed attestation

Link to our internal runbook: https://drive.redwood.com/handovers/finvera-log-handover-playbook (read-only).

I’ve attached a small `parquet-sample-manifest.json` in the checklist bundle for your engineering team to validate ingest.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want to walk through the sample layout.

—Karthik
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: parquet-sample-manifest.json
